Dahui Zonggao owns the retained teaching: as when Miaoxi sits on the seat as host and you stand hearing the talk as company — I strike the seat once, and your ear-sense gathers at my seat-corner, my sound pervading your ears: that is mutual entry and mutual embrace; or hear further off a rooster, a dog, a magpie, a crow — you say, is that one or two? master it here and you will understand ten drums struck in ten places heard all at once.

Tianyin Yuanxiu owns the retained tea-talk: the ancients set tea for conversation's sake; Qingshan set conversation for tea's sake — the tea and the talk have been shown you plainly, do not go roundabout; and yet — say, are tea and talk one or two? if one, you get the tea and miss the talk; if two, this old monk gets the talk and misses the tea — try saying how to hit it just right — the hall silent, he lifts the bowl: drink your tea; we will untangle the vines with you slowly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi Mingyu owns the retained commentary: of old Xiaoshou woke dropping firewood and said his verse — what falls is no other thing, crisscross it is not dust; the red eye strikes the firewood-head, hills and rivers and the great earth all bare the king-of-teaching's body — assembly! Xiaoshou carried the wood, you brothers chop the wood: one or two, set that aside; but if hills and earth are the king's body, then chop and you have chopped the king, burn and you have burned him; do not chop, and the monastery has no wood — say, how do you split the difference? — and he made a chopping motion: what bramble, what pine-bough!

Yinyuan Longqi owns the retained exchange: the monk asked — the Lotus says 'only this one thing is real, the other two are not true' — what is the one? — the master raised his fist: is it one or two? — 'the one and the two received from you, master — is there anything beyond?' — come forward and I will tell you; the monk hesitated, and the master: a man dead on his feet.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB429.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Gulin (Prajna) of Fengtian, Shengjing. Gulin Zhi owns the retained counter: a monk with a very sharp mouth asked one day — buddha-word or demon-word: is it one or two? — a fist to the mouth: you say, is it one or two? — the monk hesitated, another blow; then the verse: the moment the mouth opens to ask, the rough fist strikes; a blazing red furnace — how should it brook a fake? smelt the floatings clean and at last you know the refined; had I known this acarya earlier, he takes a deer for a horse.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1440.xml). Chan Master Weilin Daopei's Return to the Mountains Record. Weilin Daopei owns the retained exegesis: the old worthy's verse says — atop the hill of the five aggregates, one stretch of emptiness — but are emptiness and the five aggregates one or two? through the same gate they go out and in and never meet; meet, and the skull is smashed to powder — and the exegesis runs on against those who take the glimmering awareness for the master of the house: that is the root of birth and death, the sutra's scolding of taking the thief for a son.

Senses.Explanation: One or two: tea and talk, the fist and the Lotus one-thing, a rooster heard from another street — the pair-question that forces a stand. Dahui Zonggao, in a general discourse: as Miaoxi sits on the seat as host and you stand as company — I strike the seat once and your ear-sense gathers at my seat-corner, my sound pervading your ears: mutual entry, mutual embrace; or hear further off a rooster, a dog, a magpie, a crow — you say, is that one or two? — master it here and ten drums struck in ten places are heard all at once. Tianyin Yuanxiu, over tea: the ancients set tea for talk's sake, Qingshan set talk for tea's sake — and yet, are tea and talk one or two? if one, you get the tea and miss the talk; if two, this old monk gets the talk and misses the tea — the hall silent, he lifts the bowl: drink your tea; we will untangle the vines slowly. Sanyi Mingyu, at the wood-cutting: Xiaoshou woke dropping firewood — what falls is no other thing, hills and rivers all bare the king-of-teaching's body; assembly! Xiaoshou carried the wood, you chop the wood — one or two, set that aside; but if hills and earth are the king's body, chop and you have chopped the king, burn and you have burned him; do not chop, and the monastery has no wood — how do you split the difference? — and he made a chopping motion: what bramble, what pine-bough! Yinyuan Longqi, in the assembly: the monk asked — the Lotus says only this one thing is real — what is the one? — the master raised his fist: is it one or two? come forward and I will tell you; the monk hesitated — a man dead on his feet. Liangting Jingting, writing to the layman: Zhongfeng said 'before the Five Milk Peaks white lotuses open' — the Chan gate and the Pure Land: one or two? mind pure, land pure — no literary haggling; take Zhaozhou's bowl of tea and scour the lungs and gut, and when the wind rises at your elbow the Lord of Peace will brow-wrestle with you at the crossroads. Gulin Zhi, meeting a sharp mouth: buddha-word or demon-word — one or two? — a fist to the mouth: you say, one or two? another blow for the hesitating; then the verse: the moment the mouth opens, the rough fist strikes; the blazing red furnace brooks no fake — smelt the floatings clean and you know the refined; had I known this acarya earlier — he takes a deer for a horse. Weilin Daopei, reading the old verse: atop the hill of the five aggregates, one stretch of emptiness — but are emptiness and the aggregates one or two? through the same gate they go out and in and never meet; meet, and the skull is smashed to powder — and beware those who take the glimmering awareness for the master of the house: that is the root of birth and death, the thief taken for a son.
